transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. First, please do not attempt to regas this yourself. Refrigerant systems are sealed and under pressure; adding gas without finding and fixing a leak is illegal for DIYers in many cases, dangerous if you puncture lines, and will not fix the underlying fault. This work requires an engineer with recovery equipment. Regarding your symptoms: since the compressor is running and the back of the fridge is warm, the cooling system is likely producing cold (the compressor is pumping). The problem is usually that this cold air isn't reaching the fridge compartment. On most modern fridge-freezers, there is one evaporator coil in the freezer that cools both sections via a fan and vents. 1. A blocked airflow (usually caused by ice buildup on the evaporator coils due to a defrost system failure).
2. To tell these apart, please check: Is the freezer compartment still cold or icy, or is it warm too? Also, when you open the freezer door, can you hear a faint humming or whirring sound (the fan) running inside?
freezer is warm too, about 0C and everything's thawed. i can hear a fan going when the door's shut. no frost anywhere inside either

Because both the fridge and freezer are warm (about 0°C) while the compressor is running and the back of the unit is hot, the cooling circuit is likely failing to produce cold. This usually means either the compressor has lost its pumping efficiency or there is a leak in the sealed system. Refrigerant systems are sealed and pressurised; adding gas without finding and fixing a leak is illegal for DIYers in many cases, dangerous if you puncture lines (the gas can be flammable), and will not fix the underlying fault. This work requires a qualified refrigeration engineer with recovery equipment. Given that both compartments have warmed up significantly and there is no frost buildup to suggest an airflow blockage, this points strongly to a hardware failure in the cooling system itself. Unless you are comfortable replacing major internal components like the compressor or control board (which involves electrical work and potentially handling refrigerants), I would recommend calling an engineer for a quote. They can confirm if it is worth repairing against replacement.
